item.title: Contrasting ecological patterns across deglaciating Western Antarctic Peninsula fjords revealed by soft-sediment benthic assemblages
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04216-1

Soft-sediment benthic assemblages vary among fjords and with glacier proximity, with diversity increasing toward fjord mouths while biomass and density show fjord-specific patterns across glacier-distance gradients in three Western Antarctic Peninsula fjords.

item.title: High-resolution mapping reveals trade-offs among tea production, food security and biodiversity conservation
item.content:encoded:
Communications Earth & Environment, Published online: 12 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s43247-026-04153-z

Tea production shows uneven trade-offs among economic returns, food security, and biodiversity across major producing countries, with China achieving the strongest balance and Kenya underperforming in all three, based on 10-m satellite mapping and cross-country sustainability assessments.
item.dc:title: High-resolution mapping reveals trade-offs among tea production, food security and biodiversity conservation
